title: World map for the cocoa journey; map-and-reasoning task criteria
subject: Geography
source: Written for geography/y6 lesson 16 (World map for the cocoa journey; map-and-reasoning task criteria (portal printable; assessed))
intro: Lesson 16: Global trade: follow a cocoa bean. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

panels.title: Trade
points: The UK imports lots of food

timeline.label: Step 1
timeline.text: Farm in Ghana: pods picked, beans dried

timeline.label: Step 3
timeline.text: Factory in Europe: roasted, made into chocolate

panels.title: Who gets the money?
points: Farmers often get a small share
Fair trade aims to pay farmers fairly

model.title: Why is cocoa grown in Ghana but sold in the UK?

parts.text: Cocoa needs heat and rain all year
Ghana is near the equator: tropical
The UK is temperate: cocoa will not grow

parts.label: Why it works
parts.text: Climate decides where it grows; trade brings it here

blocks.text: Draw arrows for the cocoa beans' journey: farm, port, ship, factory, shop. Then explain one reason for each stage.

keywords.def: goods sent out of a country
all the steps from raw material to shop
trade that pays farmers a fair price

questions.q: Is a UK car sold to France an import or export for the UK?

Core (assessed map and reasoning task): Draw the cocoa journey from Ghana to the UK on the world map, label continents, oceans and four steps, then explain in the portal response box why each step happens where it does.
questions.a: Accurate route and reasoned explanation linking climate, trade and industry

questions.q: Extend: Explain how buying fair trade chocolate helps a farmer.
questions.a: A fair minimum price and a premium for the community, for example for schools or wells

questions.q: Stretch: Give one environmental cost of this supply chain.
questions.a: Ship and lorry fuel emissions; forests cleared for cocoa farms

questions.q: Cocoa beans arriving in the UK are:
questions.a: B) Imports. Goods coming into the UK are imports.
All the steps from raw material to shop
options: All the steps from raw material to shop

questions.q: Big question: how many countries helped make your chocolate?
questions.a: Several: grown in West Africa, shipped, made in Europe and sold in the UK
